title: How close are we to holographic environments?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss how close holographic environments are to reality, starting from the Star Trek holodeck and moving to telepresence/tele-immersion for video conferencing, the National Tele-Immersion Initiative, ultra-fast internet (the Internet2-style university network), Microsoft's HoloDesk research, Microsoft Kinect motion tracking, haptic feedback for virtual touch and hugging, the 2Pac hologram at Coachella, and PTSD training uses. They also read a listener email from Lance Spangler about supercomputer nuclear simulations and cell-level heart modeling.

entities.name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

segments.title: Opening banter and Chuck's mustache fundraiser
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with off-topic banter about the dinosaur toy and Chuck's Movember mustache fundraiser for prostate cancer research, then introduce the topic Chuck picked.

segments.title: The holodeck and what tele-immersion means
segments.summary: The hosts compare the Star Trek holodeck with the Star Wars projected hologram, explaining that tele-immersion aims for three-dimensional, 360-degree interactive projections where people can move around and interact, not just watch a clunky projection.

segments.title: Telepresence, video conferencing and the 2000 breakthrough
segments.summary: They discuss tele-immersion as a replacement for video conferencing and travel, the Tandberg system that was already HD, and the limits of webcams such as eye contact and tracking. They describe the National Tele-Immersion Initiative's 2000 breakthrough showing 3D holographic images of colleagues in different cities.

segments.title: Bandwidth challenges and ultra-fast networks
segments.summary: The hosts describe the data demands of tele-immersion, including frame refresh rates, and mention a university initiative to build much faster networks, including for underserved rural areas.

segments.title: Microsoft HoloDesk and haptics
segments.summary: Josh describes Microsoft's HoloDesk research project, which projects 2D images through a half-silvered beam splitter onto a desk so users can juggle virtual balls. They then discuss haptic feedback as a way to simulate touch, such as vibrating game controllers and tactile sensors, and virtual hugging.

segments.title: Training uses, Kinect and the 2Pac hologram
segments.summary: The hosts discuss surgeon and soldier training and a PTSD-prevention idea of desensitizing soldiers through immersive simulation. They mention Microsoft's Kinect motion tracking and then the 2Pac hologram, which used a projection and reflective screen setup to perform alongside live performers.

segments.title: Wrap-up and Berkeley tele-immersion lab
segments.summary: The hosts close the topic, mention that Berkeley's tele-immersion lab is still active (Josh briefly confuses the school with a Massachusetts one), and joke about a future where a boss hugs remotely.

segments.title: Listener mail from Lance Spangler
segments.summary: Chuck reads an email from listener Lance Spangler, who writes about a California supercomputer that simulates nuclear weapons at the sub-atomic level and models human heart cells to test drugs and diseases. The hosts also discuss sending stickers and shirts to military listeners.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact info
segments.summary: Josh gives contact details for Twitter, Facebook, and email, and points listeners to HowStuffWorks.com.
